research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and National Data Library sources only; PFA/CSP geography, rate calculation, revisions, classification breaks and rural-urban context; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: BTP exclusion from CSP tables
verified_claims: British Transport Police data are excluded from CSP-level data
this exclusion contributes to differences from national totals
limitations: BTP incidents must not be silently assigned to territorial CSPs
PFA and CSP scope must be compared before aggregation

sources.name: PFA crime-rate denominator
verified_claims: PFA crime rates can be calculated with ONS population estimates
the numerator comes from police-recorded-crime counts
limitations: population edition and geography must match the crime period
rates are not direct measures of victimisation risk

sources.name: CSP crime-rate denominator
verified_claims: CSP crime rates can be calculated with ONS local-authority population estimates
the CSP geography generally follows local-authority boundaries
limitations: combined or non-coterminous CSPs require denominator reconciliation
population denominators are not parcel counts

sources.name: Crime-rate per-thousand convention
verified_claims: crime rates are typically expressed per 1,000 population
the convention is used because many crime types have low volumes
limitations: the denominator convention must be displayed
different rate bases must not be compared without conversion

sources.name: Crime-rate formula
verified_claims: the guide defines rate calculation as crimes divided by population multiplied by 1,000
the formula applies to matching area and period
limitations: zero or missing denominators must fail closed
counts and rates must be stored as different measures

sources.name: ONS CSP-rate publication
verified_claims: ONS publishes rates for main crime types at CSP level
the official rate tables can be used instead of recomputing where available
limitations: published rates retain ONS definitions and revisions
main crime types do not cover every offence code

sources.name: ONS PFA Table P1 rates
verified_claims: PFA-level rates are available in ONS table P1
the table belongs to the Police Force Area data-table release
limitations: table edition must match the crime period
PFA rates are not CSP or parcel rates

sources.name: Quarterly revision cycle
verified_claims: quarterly police-recorded-crime figures are revised every quarter
revisions reflect the live administrative nature of the data
limitations: quarterly values require edition metadata
a revised quarter must replace rather than duplicate its predecessor

sources.name: Transfer-driven crime deletion
verified_claims: a recorded crime can later be deleted when transferred to another PFA
the deletion changes previously supplied quarterly figures
limitations: transfer deletion is not evidence that no incident occurred
origin and destination records must not be double counted

sources.name: Cancellation-driven crime deletion
verified_claims: a recorded crime can later be deleted when it is cancelled
cancellation contributes to quarterly revisions
limitations: cancellation categories require official reason metadata
deleted records must not be retained as current offences
